excerpt: In September 2023, we released our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP), a public commitment not to train or deploy models capable of causing catastrophic harm unless we have implemented safety and security measures that will keep risks below acceptable levels.
paraphrase: Anthropic states it released the RSP in September 2023 as a public commitment not to train or deploy catastrophically dangerous models without adequate safety and security measures.

excerpt: We are now updating our RSP to account for the lessons we’ve learned over the last year.
paraphrase: Anthropic explains that the RSP is being updated based on lessons learned over the past year.

excerpt: This updated policy reflects our view that risk governance in this rapidly evolving domain should be proportional, iterative, and exportable.
paraphrase: Anthropic states its view that risk governance should be proportional, iterative, and exportable.

excerpt: AI Safety Level Standards (ASL Standards) are a set of technical and operational measures for safely training and deploying frontier AI models. These currently fall into two categories: Deployment Standards and Security Standards.
paraphrase: ASL Standards are defined as technical and operational measures for safe training and deployment, divided into Deployment and Security Standards.

excerpt: As model capabilities increase, so will the need for stronger safeguards, which are captured in successively higher ASL Standards.
paraphrase: Increasing model capability requires progressively stronger safeguards, reflected in higher ASL Standards.

excerpt: At present, all of our models must meet the ASL-2 Deployment and Security Standards.
paraphrase: Currently all Anthropic models are required to meet ASL-2 Deployment and Security Standards.

excerpt: To determine when a model has become sufficiently advanced such that its deployment and security measures should be strengthened, we use the concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic uses Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards to determine when to strengthen deployment and security measures.

excerpt: A Capability Threshold tells us when we need to upgrade our protections, and the corresponding Required Safeguards tell us what standard should apply.
paraphrase: Capability Thresholds signal when protections must be upgraded, while Required Safeguards define the applicable standard.

locator: Executive Summary / Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards
excerpt: The Required Safeguards for each Capability Threshold are intended to mitigate risk to acceptable levels.
paraphrase: Required Safeguards for each threshold aim to bring risk down to acceptable levels.

locator: Executive Summary / Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards
excerpt: This update to our RSP provides specifications for Capabilities Thresholds related to Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) weapons and Autonomous AI Research and Development (AI R&D) and identifies the corresponding Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: This RSP update specifies Capability Thresholds for CBRN weapons and Autonomous AI R&D, along with their Required Safeguards.

excerpt: We will routinely test models to determine whether their capabilities fall sufficiently far below the Capability Thresholds such that the ASL-2 Standard remains appropriate.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to routine testing to check whether models remain sufficiently below Capability Thresholds for ASL-2 to remain appropriate.

excerpt: We will first conduct preliminary assessments to determine whether a more comprehensive evaluation is needed.
paraphrase: Preliminary assessments will first be conducted to decide if comprehensive evaluation is warranted.

excerpt: For models requiring comprehensive testing, we will assess whether the model is unlikely to reach any relevant Capability Thresholds absent surprising advances in widely accessible post-training enhancements.
paraphrase: For models needing comprehensive testing, Anthropic will assess whether the model is unlikely to reach relevant thresholds absent unexpected post-training advances.

excerpt: If, after the comprehensive testing, we determine that the model is sufficiently below the relevant Capability Thresholds, then we will continue to apply the ASL-2 Standard.
paraphrase: If comprehensive testing shows the model is sufficiently below thresholds, ASL-2 continues to apply.

excerpt: If, however, we are unable to make the required showing, we will act as though the model has surpassed the Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: If Anthropic cannot show the model is sufficiently below the threshold, it will treat the model as having surpassed it.

excerpt: This means that we will both upgrade to the ASL-3 Required Safeguards and conduct a follow-up capability assessment to confirm that the ASL-4 Standard is not necessary.
paraphrase: Treating the model as having surpassed the threshold means upgrading to ASL-3 safeguards and conducting a follow-up assessment to rule out the need for ASL-4.

excerpt: To determine whether the measures we have adopted satisfy the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, we will conduct a safeguards assessment.
paraphrase: A safeguards assessment will be conducted to check whether adopted measures satisfy ASL-3 requirements.

excerpt: For the ASL-3 Deployment Standard, we will evaluate whether it is robust to persistent attempts to misuse the capability in question.
paraphrase: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard will be evaluated for robustness against persistent misuse attempts.

excerpt: For the ASL-3 Security Standard, we will evaluate whether it is highly protected against non-state attackers attempting to steal model weights.
paraphrase: The ASL-3 Security Standard will be evaluated for high protection against non-state actors attempting to steal model weights.

excerpt: If we determine that we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, then we will proceed to deployment, provided we have also conducted a follow-up capability assessment.
paraphrase: If ASL-3 safeguards are met and a follow-up capability assessment has been conducted, Anthropic will proceed with deployment.

excerpt: In parallel with upgrading a model to the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, we will conduct a follow-up capability assessment to confirm that further safeguards are not necessary.
paraphrase: While upgrading to ASL-3 safeguards, a follow-up capability assessment will confirm whether further safeguards are needed.

excerpt: We are currently working on defining any further Capability Thresholds that would mandate ASL-4 Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic is still working on defining further Capability Thresholds that would require ASL-4 safeguards.

locator: Executive Summary / Deployment and scaling outcomes
excerpt: We may deploy or store a model if either of the following criteria are met: (1) the model’s capabilities are sufficiently far away from the existing Capability Thresholds, making the current ASL-2 Standard appropriate; or (2) the model’s capabilities have surpassed the existing Capabilities Threshold, but we have implemented the ASL-3 Required Safeguards and conducted the follow-up capability assessment.
paraphrase: A model may be deployed or stored if it is sufficiently below Capability Thresholds under ASL-2, or if it has surpassed the threshold but ASL-3 safeguards and follow-up assessment have been completed.

locator: Executive Summary / Deployment and scaling outcomes
excerpt: In any scenario where we determine that a model requires ASL-3 Required Safeguards but we are unable to implement them immediately, we will act promptly to reduce interim risk to acceptable levels until the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are in place.
paraphrase: If ASL-3 safeguards are required but cannot be implemented immediately, Anthropic will act promptly to reduce interim risk until they are in place.

excerpt: To facilitate the effective implementation of this policy across the company, we commit to several internal governance measures, including maintaining the position of Responsible Scaling Officer, establishing a process through which Anthropic staff may anonymously notify the Responsible Scaling Officer of any potential instances of noncompliance, and developing internal safety procedures for incident scenarios.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to internal governance measures including a Responsible Scaling Officer role, an anonymous noncompliance reporting process, and internal incident procedures.

excerpt: To advance the public dialogue on the regulation of frontier AI model risks and to enable examination of our actions, we will also publicly release key materials related to the evaluation and deployment of our models with sensitive information removed and solicit input from external experts in relevant domains.
paraphrase: Anthropic will publicly release evaluation and deployment materials (redacted of sensitive information) and seek external expert input to support public dialogue and scrutiny.

excerpt: As frontier AI models advance, we believe they will bring about transformative benefits for our society and economy.
paraphrase: Anthropic believes advancing frontier AI models will bring transformative societal and economic benefits.

excerpt: AI could accelerate scientific discoveries, revolutionize healthcare, enhance our education system, and create entirely new domains for human creativity and innovation.
paraphrase: AI is expected to accelerate science, transform healthcare, improve education, and enable new creative domains.

excerpt: Frontier AI models also, however, present new challenges and risks that warrant careful study and effective safeguards.
paraphrase: Frontier AI models also pose new risks requiring careful study and effective safeguards.

excerpt: In September 2023, we released our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP), a first-of-its-kind public commitment not to train or deploy models capable of causing catastrophic harm unless we have implemented safety and security measures that will keep risks below acceptable levels.
paraphrase: Anthropic describes the September 2023 RSP release as a first-of-its-kind commitment not to train or deploy catastrophically dangerous models without adequate safeguards.

excerpt: Our RSP serves several purposes: it is an internal operating procedure for investigating and mitigating these risks and helps inform the public of our plans and commitments.
paraphrase: The RSP functions both as an internal risk-mitigation procedure and as public communication of Anthropic's plans.

excerpt: We also hope it will serve as a prototype for other companies looking to adopt similar frameworks and, potentially, inform regulators about possible best practices.
paraphrase: Anthropic hopes the RSP can be a model for other companies and inform regulatory best practices.

excerpt: We are now updating our RSP to account for the lessons we’ve learned over the last year.
paraphrase: The RSP is being updated to reflect lessons learned over the past year.

excerpt: This policy reflects our view that risk governance in this rapidly evolving domain should be proportional, iterative, and exportable.
paraphrase: The updated policy embodies the view that risk governance should be proportional, iterative, and exportable.

excerpt: First, our approach to risk should be proportional.
paraphrase: Anthropic states its first principle: risk approach should be proportional.

excerpt: Central to our policy is the concept of AI Safety Level Standards: technical and operational standards for safely training and deploying frontier models that correspond with a particular level of risk.
paraphrase: ASL Standards, which correspond to levels of risk, are central to the policy.

excerpt: By implementing safeguards that are proportional to the nature and extent of an AI model’s risks, we can balance innovation with safety, maintaining rigorous protections without unnecessarily hindering progress.
paraphrase: Proportional safeguards allow balancing innovation and safety without unduly hindering progress.

excerpt: This approach also enables us to allocate resources efficiently, focusing our most stringent safeguards on the models that pose the greater risk, while affording more flexibility for lower-risk systems.
paraphrase: Proportionality allows efficient resource allocation, concentrating strict safeguards on higher-risk models and more flexibility for lower-risk ones.

excerpt: Second, our approach to risk should be iterative.
paraphrase: Anthropic's second principle is that risk approach should be iterative.

excerpt: Since the frontier of AI is rapidly evolving, we cannot anticipate what safety and security measures will be appropriate for models far beyond the current frontier.
paraphrase: Because AI is evolving rapidly, Anthropic cannot predict what safety measures will suit far future models.

excerpt: We will thus regularly measure the capability of our models and adjust our safeguards accordingly.
paraphrase: Anthropic will regularly measure model capability and adjust safeguards accordingly.

excerpt: Further, we will continue to research potential risks and next-generation mitigation techniques.
paraphrase: Anthropic will continue researching potential risks and future mitigation techniques.

excerpt: And, at the highest level of generality, we will look for opportunities to improve and strengthen our overarching risk management framework.
paraphrase: At the broadest level, Anthropic will seek opportunities to improve its overall risk management framework.

excerpt: Third, our approach to risk should be exportable.
paraphrase: Anthropic's third principle is that its risk approach should be exportable.

excerpt: To demonstrate that it is possible to balance innovation with safety, we must put forward our proof of concept: a pragmatic, flexible, and scalable approach to risk governance.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims to demonstrate a pragmatic, flexible, scalable risk governance approach as proof that innovation and safety can be balanced.

excerpt: By sharing our approach externally, we aim to set a new industry standard that encourages widespread adoption of similar frameworks.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims to set an industry standard by sharing its approach externally to encourage similar frameworks elsewhere.

excerpt: In the long term, we hope that our policy may offer relevant insights for regulation.
paraphrase: Anthropic hopes the policy will inform future regulation in the long term.

excerpt: In the meantime, we will continue to share our findings with policymakers.
paraphrase: Anthropic will continue sharing findings with policymakers in the meantime.

excerpt: Although this policy focuses on catastrophic risks, they are not the only risks that we consider important.
paraphrase: The policy focuses on catastrophic risks, but Anthropic considers other risks important too.

excerpt: Our Usage Policy sets forth our standards for the use of our products, including prohibitions on using our models to spread misinformation, incite violence or hateful behavior, or engage in fraudulent or abusive practices, and we continually refine our technical measures for enforcing our trust and safety standards at scale.
paraphrase: The Usage Policy prohibits misuse such as misinformation, incitement, and fraud, and Anthropic continually refines enforcement measures at scale.

excerpt: Further, we conduct research to understand the broader societal impacts of our models.
paraphrase: Anthropic conducts research into the broader societal impacts of its models.

excerpt: Our Responsible Scaling Policy complements our work in these areas, contributing to our understanding of current and potential risks.
paraphrase: The RSP complements other work areas by contributing to understanding of current and potential risks.

excerpt: At Anthropic, we are committed to developing AI responsibly and transparently.
paraphrase: Anthropic states its commitment to responsible and transparent AI development.

excerpt: Since our founding, we have recognized the importance of proactively addressing potential risks as we push the boundaries of AI capability and of clearly communicating about the nature and extent of those risks.
paraphrase: Since its founding, Anthropic has emphasized proactively addressing risks while advancing AI capability and clearly communicating about those risks.

excerpt: We look forward to continuing to refine our approach to risk governance and to collaborating with stakeholders across the AI ecosystem.
paraphrase: Anthropic looks forward to continuing refinement of risk governance and collaboration with the wider AI ecosystem.

excerpt: This policy is designed in the spirit of the Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) framework introduced by the non-profit AI safety organization METR, as well as emerging government policy proposals in the UK, EU, and US.
paraphrase: The policy is inspired by METR's RSP framework and by emerging government proposals in the UK, EU, and US.

excerpt: This policy also helps satisfy our Voluntary White House Commitments (2023) and Frontier AI Safety Commitments (2024).
paraphrase: The policy also helps fulfill Anthropic's 2023 Voluntary White House Commitments and 2024 Frontier AI Safety Commitments.

excerpt: We extend our sincere gratitude to the many external groups that provided invaluable guidance on the development and refinement of our Responsible Scaling Policy.
paraphrase: Anthropic thanks external groups for guidance on developing and refining the RSP.

excerpt: We actively welcome feedback on our policy and suggestions for improvement from other entities engaged in frontier AI risk evaluations or safety and security standards.
paraphrase: Anthropic invites feedback and improvement suggestions from other entities engaged in frontier AI risk work.

excerpt: To submit your feedback or suggestions, please contact us at rsp@anthropic.com.
paraphrase: Anthropic provides a contact email for feedback and suggestions.

excerpt: AI Safety Level Standards (ASL Standards) are core to our risk mitigation strategy.
paraphrase: ASL Standards are described as central to Anthropic's risk mitigation strategy.

excerpt: An ASL Standard is a set of technical and operational measures for safely training and deploying frontier AI models.
paraphrase: An ASL Standard consists of technical and operational measures for safe training and deployment of frontier models.

excerpt: As model capabilities increase, so will the need for stronger safeguards, which are captured in successively higher ASL Standards.
paraphrase: Stronger safeguards are needed as capabilities grow, reflected in higher ASL Standards.

excerpt: Definitions of ASL Standards and other key terms are available in Appendix A.
paraphrase: Definitions of ASL Standards and other terms appear in Appendix A.

excerpt: The types of measures that compose an ASL Standard currently fall into two categories–Deployment Standards and Security Standards–which map onto the types of risks that frontier AI models may pose.
paraphrase: ASL Standard measures are currently divided into Deployment Standards and Security Standards, corresponding to different risk types.

excerpt: Deployment Standards: Deployment Standards are technical, operational, and policy measures to ensure the safe usage of AI models by external users (i.e., our users and customers) as well as internal users (i.e., our employees).
paraphrase: Deployment Standards are measures ensuring safe use of models by both external and internal users.

excerpt: Deployment Standards aim to strike a balance between enabling beneficial use of AI technologies and mitigating the risks of potentially catastrophic cases of misuse.
paraphrase: Deployment Standards seek to balance beneficial use with mitigation of catastrophic misuse risks.

excerpt: Security Standards: Security Standards are technical, operational, and policy measures to protect AI models–particularly their weights and associated systems–from unauthorized access, theft, or compromise by malicious actors.
paraphrase: Security Standards protect AI models, especially weights and associated systems, from unauthorized access, theft, or compromise.

excerpt: Security Standards are intended to maintain the integrity and controlled use of AI models throughout their lifecycle, from development to deployment.
paraphrase: Security Standards aim to maintain model integrity and controlled use throughout the lifecycle.

excerpt: We expect to continue refining our framework in response to future risks (for example, the risk that an AI system attempts to subvert the goals of its operators).
paraphrase: Anthropic expects to keep refining the framework in response to future risks, such as an AI subverting operator goals.

excerpt: At present, all of our models must meet the ASL-2 Deployment and Security Standards.
paraphrase: All current models must currently meet ASL-2 Deployment and Security Standards.

excerpt: The ASL-2 Security and Deployment Standards provide a baseline level of safe deployment and model security for AI models.
paraphrase: ASL-2 Standards provide baseline safety and security for AI models.

excerpt: These standards, which are summarized below, are available in full in Appendix B.
paraphrase: Full ASL-2 standards are provided in Appendix B, with a summary here.

excerpt: The ASL-2 Deployment Standard reduces the prevalence of misuse, and includes the publication of model cards and enforcement of Usage Policy; harmlessness training such as Constitutional AI and automated detection mechanisms; and establishing vulnerability reporting channels as well as a bug bounty for universal jailbreaks.
paraphrase: The ASL-2 Deployment Standard reduces misuse through model card publication, Usage Policy enforcement, harmlessness training, automated detection, vulnerability reporting, and a jailbreak bug bounty.

excerpt: The ASL-2 Security Standard requires a security system that can likely thwart most opportunistic attackers and includes vendor and supplier security reviews, physical security measures, and the use of secure-by-design principles.
paraphrase: The ASL-2 Security Standard requires defenses against most opportunistic attackers, including vendor reviews, physical security, and secure-by-design practices.

excerpt: Although the ASL-2 Standard is appropriate for all of our current models, that may not hold true in the future as our models become more capable.
paraphrase: ASL-2 fits current models but may not remain adequate as capabilities increase.

excerpt: To determine when a model has become sufficiently advanced such that its deployment and security measures should be strengthened, we use the concepts of Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards determine when deployment and security measures should strengthen.

excerpt: A Capability Threshold tells us when we need to upgrade our protections, and the corresponding Required Safeguards tell us what standard should apply.
paraphrase: A Capability Threshold signals when protections need upgrading; Required Safeguards specify the applicable standard.

excerpt: A Capability Threshold is a prespecified level of AI capability that, if reached, signals (1) a meaningful increase in the level of risk if the model remains under the existing set of safeguards (2) a corresponding need to upgrade the safeguards to a higher ASL Standard.
paraphrase: A Capability Threshold is a predefined capability level whose attainment signals meaningfully increased risk and the need for higher-level safeguards.

excerpt: In other words, a Capability Threshold serves as a trigger for shifting from an ASL-N Standard to an ASL-N+1 Standard (or, in some cases, moving straight to ASL N+2 or higher).
paraphrase: A Capability Threshold triggers movement from one ASL level to the next, or occasionally to a higher one.

excerpt: Depending on the Capability Threshold, it may not be necessary to upgrade both the Deployment and Security Standards; each Capability Threshold corresponds to specific Required Safeguards that identify which of the ASL Standards must be met.
paraphrase: Not every Capability Threshold requires upgrading both Deployment and Security Standards; each threshold has specific Required Safeguards indicating which standards apply.

excerpt: Below, we specify the Capability Thresholds and their corresponding Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: This section specifies Capability Thresholds and their Required Safeguards.

excerpt: The Required Safeguards for each Capability Threshold are intended to mitigate risk from a model with such capabilities to acceptable levels.
paraphrase: Required Safeguards aim to reduce risk from models at each threshold to acceptable levels.

excerpt: In developing these standards, we have weighed the risks and benefits of frontier model development.
paraphrase: Anthropic weighed risks and benefits of frontier model development in creating these standards.

excerpt: We believe these safeguards are achievable with sufficient investment and advance planning into research and development and would advocate for the industry as a whole to adopt them.
paraphrase: Anthropic believes the safeguards are achievable with sufficient investment and planning, and advocates industry-wide adoption.

excerpt: We will conduct assessments to inform when to implement the Required Safeguards (see Section 4).
paraphrase: Assessments will determine timing for implementing Required Safeguards.

excerpt: The Capability Thresholds summarized below are available in full in Appendix C.
paraphrase: Full detail on the summarized Capability Thresholds is in Appendix C.

excerpt: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) weapons. The ability to significantly help individuals or groups with basic technical backgrounds (e.g., undergraduate STEM degrees) create/obtain and deploy CBRN weapons.
paraphrase: The CBRN Capability Threshold is defined as significantly helping individuals or groups with basic technical backgrounds create/obtain and deploy CBRN weapons.

paraphrase: The CBRN capability could greatly expand the pool of actors able to cause harm, without a corresponding defensive improvement.

paraphrase: ASL-3 Deployment and Security Standards, guarding against misuse and non-state weight theft, are required for the CBRN threshold.

excerpt: Autonomous AI Research and Development (AI R&D): The ability to either fully automate the work of an entry-level remote-only Researcher at Anthropic, or cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling.
paraphrase: The AI R&D threshold is defined as fully automating an entry-level remote researcher's work, or causing dramatic acceleration of effective scaling.

excerpt: This capability could greatly increase the pace of AI development, potentially leading to rapid and unpredictable advances in AI capabilities and associated risks.
paraphrase: This capability risks greatly speeding up AI development, causing rapid unpredictable advances and associated risks.

context_stem: Row: Autonomous AI Research and Development (AI R&D); Column: Required Safeguards
excerpt: At minimum, the ASL-3 Security Standard is required, although we expect a higher security standard (which would protect against model-weight theft by state-level adversaries) will be required, especially in the case of dramatic acceleration.
paraphrase: At minimum ASL-3 Security is required, but a higher standard protecting against state-level weight theft is expected, especially with dramatic acceleration.

locator: Table: Capability Thresholds / AI R&D / Required Safeguards
context_stem: Row: Autonomous AI Research and Development (AI R&D); Column: Required Safeguards
excerpt: We also expect a strong affirmative case (made with accountability for both the reasoning and implementation) about the risk of models pursuing misaligned goals will be required.
paraphrase: A strong affirmative case regarding the risk of misaligned goal pursuit, with accountability for reasoning and implementation, is also expected to be required.

excerpt: We will specify these requirements more precisely when we reach the 2-8 hour software engineering tasks checkpoint.
paraphrase: More precise requirement specification will occur upon reaching the 2-8 hour software engineering tasks checkpoint.

excerpt: We will consider it sufficient to rule out the possibility that a model has surpassed the Autonomous AI R&D Capability Threshold by considering an earlier (i.e., less capable) checkpoint: the ability to autonomously perform a wide range of 2-8 hour software engineering tasks.
paraphrase: Ruling out surpassing the AI R&D threshold will rely on an earlier checkpoint: autonomous performance of a wide range of 2-8 hour software engineering tasks.

excerpt: We would view this level of capability as an important checkpoint towards both Autonomous AI R&D as well as other capabilities that may warrant similar attention (for example, autonomous replication).
paraphrase: This checkpoint is viewed as important toward Autonomous AI R&D and other capabilities warranting similar attention, such as autonomous replication.

excerpt: We will test for this checkpoint and, by the time we reach it, we aim to have met (or be close to meeting) the ASL-3 Security Standard as an intermediate goal, and we will share an update on our progress around that time.
paraphrase: Anthropic will test for this checkpoint and aims to have met or nearly met ASL-3 Security by then, sharing a progress update around that time.

excerpt: At that point, we will also specify Required Safeguards for this Capability Threshold in more detail, update our list of Capability Thresholds to consider additional risks that may arise, and test for the full Autonomous AI R&D Capability Threshold and any additional risks.
paraphrase: At that point, Required Safeguards will be detailed further, the Capability Thresholds list updated for new risks, and testing conducted for the full AI R&D threshold and additional risks.

excerpt: We will also maintain a list of capabilities that we think require significant investigation and may require stronger safeguards than ASL-2 provides.
paraphrase: A list of capabilities requiring further investigation and possibly stronger-than-ASL-2 safeguards will be maintained.

excerpt: This group of capabilities could pose serious risks, but the exact Capability Threshold and the Required Safeguards are not clear at present.
paraphrase: These capabilities could pose serious risks, though the precise threshold and safeguards remain undefined.

excerpt: These capabilities may warrant a higher standard of safeguards, such as the ASL-3 Security or Deployment Standard.
paraphrase: These capabilities might require a higher safeguard standard such as ASL-3 Security or Deployment.

excerpt: However, it is also possible that by the time these capabilities are reached, there will be evidence that such a standard is not necessary (for example, because of the potential use of similar capabilities for defensive purposes).
paraphrase: Alternatively, evidence may emerge by the time these capabilities are reached showing that a higher standard is unnecessary, e.g. due to defensive uses.

excerpt: Instead of prespecifying particular thresholds and safeguards today, we will conduct ongoing assessments of the risks with the goal of determining in a future iteration of this policy what the Capability Thresholds and Required Safeguards would be.
paraphrase: Rather than prespecifying thresholds and safeguards now, ongoing risk assessments will inform future policy iterations defining them.

paraphrase: Cyber Operations capability is defined as significantly enhancing or automating sophisticated destructive cyber attacks, including novel exploit discovery, malware development, and network intrusion.

paraphrase: Assessment will involve expert engagement on cyber threat enhancement/mitigation potential and considering tiered access or phased deployment for advanced cyber capabilities.

excerpt: We will conduct either pre- or post-deployment testing, including specialized evaluations.
paraphrase: Either pre- or post-deployment testing, including specialized evaluations, will be conducted for cyber operations capability.

paraphrase: Salient results for cyber operations will be documented alongside Capability Reports.

paraphrase: Updates are hoped to be published roughly every six months.

paraphrase: Prioritization of the listed capabilities draws on commissioned research, expert discussions, forecaster input, public research, Frontier Model Forum conversations, and internal discussion.

paraphrase: Anthropic commits to refining its approach as the field and its understanding evolve.

paraphrase: Anthropic acknowledges potential risks posed by highly persuasive AI models.

paraphrase: Despite active expert consultation, persuasive AI capability is considered not yet understood enough to include in current commitments.

paraphrase: Routine testing will confirm whether models remain sufficiently below Capability Thresholds so ASL-2 remains appropriate.

paraphrase: Preliminary assessments on new and existing models, as needed, will determine whether comprehensive evaluation is required.

paraphrase: The preliminary assessment's purpose is to determine whether the model is notably more capable than the last comprehensively assessed model.

paraphrase: The Responsible Scaling Officer may also decide, at their discretion, that a comprehensive assessment is warranted.

paraphrase: No further testing is required if a model falls below the "notably more capable" standard.

excerpt: For models requiring comprehensive testing, we will assess whether the model is unlikely to reach any relevant Capability Thresholds absent surprising advances in widely accessible post-training enhancements.
paraphrase: For models needing comprehensive testing, Anthropic assesses the unlikelihood of reaching relevant thresholds absent unexpected post-training advances.

excerpt: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
paraphrase: Certain criteria must be satisfied to make the required showing.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Threat model mapping: For each capability threshold, make a compelling case that we have mapped out the most likely and consequential threat models: combinations of actors (if relevant), attack pathways, model capability bottlenecks, and types of harms.
paraphrase: One criterion is threat model mapping: making a compelling case that the most likely and consequential threat models have been identified, covering actors, attack pathways, bottlenecks, and harm types.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria: (Threat model mapping)
excerpt: We also make a compelling case that there does not exist a threat model that we are not evaluating that represents a substantial amount of risk.
paraphrase: A compelling case must also be made that no unevaluated threat model represents substantial risk.

excerpt: “Effective Compute” is a scaling-trend-based metric that accounts for both FLOPs and algorithmic improvements.
paraphrase: Effective Compute is defined as a scaling-trend-based metric incorporating both FLOPs and algorithmic improvements.

excerpt: An Effective Compute increase of K represents a performance improvement from a pretrained model on relevant task(s) equivalent to scaling up the baseline model’s training compute by a factor of K.
paraphrase: An Effective Compute increase of factor K equals a performance improvement equivalent to scaling baseline training compute by K.

excerpt: We plan to track Effective Compute during pretraining on a weighted aggregation of datasets relevant to our Capability Thresholds (e.g., coding and science).
paraphrase: Effective Compute will be tracked during pretraining using a weighted aggregation of datasets relevant to the Capability Thresholds, such as coding and science.

excerpt: This is, however, an open research question, and we will explore different possible methods.
paraphrase: This tracking approach is an open research question, and different methods will be explored.

excerpt: More generally, the Effective Compute concept is fairly new, and we may replace it with another metric in a similar spirit in the future.
paraphrase: The Effective Compute concept is new and may be replaced by a similar future metric.

excerpt: This is a broad category, including techniques like improved prompting and agent scaffolding.
paraphrase: The finetuning/elicitation category broadly includes techniques such as improved prompting and agent scaffolding.

excerpt: Exploring ways to integrate these types of improvements into an overall metric is an ongoing area of research.
paraphrase: Ongoing research explores integrating these improvements into an overall metric.

excerpt: By “widely accessible,” we mean techniques that are available to a moderately resourced group (i.e., do not involve setting up large amounts of custom infrastructure or using confidential information).
paraphrase: "Widely accessible" refers to techniques available to a moderately resourced group, not requiring extensive custom infrastructure or confidential information.

excerpt: We include headroom to account for the possibility that the model is either modified via one of our own finetuning products or stolen in the months following testing, and used to create a model that has reached a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Headroom accounts for the possibility of the model being finetuned via Anthropic's own products or stolen post-testing and used to reach a Capability Threshold.

excerpt: That said, estimating these future effects is very difficult given the state of research today.
paraphrase: Estimating these future effects remains very difficult given current research limits.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Evaluations: Design and run empirical tests that provide strong evidence that the model does not have the requisite skills; explain why the tests yielded such results; and check at test time that the results are attributable to the model’s capabilities rather than issues with the test design.
paraphrase: The evaluations criterion requires designing empirical tests providing strong evidence of lacking skills, explaining results, and confirming attribution to capability rather than test design flaws.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria: (Evaluations)
excerpt: Findings from partner organizations and external evaluations of our models (or similar models) should also be incorporated into the final assessment, when available.
paraphrase: Findings from partner organizations and external evaluations should also be incorporated into the final assessment when available.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Elicitation: Demonstrate that, when given enough resources to extrapolate to realistic attackers, researchers cannot elicit sufficiently useful results from the model on the relevant tasks.
paraphrase: The elicitation criterion requires demonstrating that researchers, given realistic attacker-level resources, cannot elicit sufficiently useful results from the model.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria: (Elicitation)
excerpt: We should assume that jailbreaks and model weight theft are possibilities, and therefore perform testing on models without safety mechanisms (such as harmlessness training) that could obscure these capabilities.
paraphrase: Testing should assume jailbreaks and weight theft are possible and be performed on models without safety mechanisms that might mask capabilities.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria: (Elicitation)
excerpt: We will also consider the possible performance increase from using resources that a realistic attacker would have access to, such as scaffolding, finetuning, and expert prompting.
paraphrase: Possible performance increases from resources a realistic attacker could access—scaffolding, finetuning, expert prompting—will also be considered.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria: (Elicitation)
excerpt: At minimum, we will perform basic finetuning for instruction following, tool use, minimizing refusal rates.
paraphrase: At minimum, basic finetuning for instruction following, tool use, and reduced refusal rates will be performed.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Forecasting: Make informal forecasts about the likelihood that further training and elicitation will improve test results between the time of testing and the next expected round of comprehensive testing.
paraphrase: The forecasting criterion requires informal forecasts on whether further training/elicitation could improve results before the next comprehensive testing round.

excerpt: Currently, these will be informal estimates of (1) the extent to which widely available elicitation techniques may improve and (2) how the model will perform on the same tasks when the next round of testing begins.
paraphrase: Forecasts currently consist of informal estimates about elicitation technique improvement and future model performance at the next testing round.

excerpt: As these are open research questions, we will aim to improve these forecasts over time so that they can be relied upon for risk judgments.
paraphrase: As open research questions, these forecasts will be improved over time to become reliable for risk judgments.

excerpt: This testing and the subsequent capability decision should ideally be concluded within about a month of reaching the “notably more capable” threshold.
paraphrase: Testing and the resulting capability decision should ideally conclude within about a month of reaching the "notably more capable" threshold.

excerpt: If, after the comprehensive testing, we determine that the model is sufficiently below the relevant Capability Thresholds, then we will continue to apply the ASL-2 Standard.
paraphrase: If the model is found sufficiently below the thresholds after comprehensive testing, ASL-2 continues to apply.

excerpt: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
paraphrase: The process for making this determination is described below.

context_stem: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
excerpt: First, we will compile a Capability Report that documents the findings from the comprehensive assessment, makes an affirmative case for why the Capability Threshold is sufficiently far away, and advances recommendations on deployment decisions.
paraphrase: A Capability Report is first compiled, documenting findings, making an affirmative case on threshold distance, and recommending deployment decisions.

context_stem: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
excerpt: The report will be escalated to the CEO and the Responsible Scaling Officer, who will (1) make the ultimate determination as to whether we have sufficiently established that we are unlikely to reach the Capability Threshold and (2) decide any deployment-related issues.
paraphrase: The Capability Report is escalated to the CEO and RSO, who make the final threshold determination and decide deployment issues.

context_stem: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
excerpt: In general, as noted in Sections 7.1.4 and 7.2.2, we will solicit both internal and external expert feedback on the report as well as the CEO and RSO’s conclusions to inform future refinements to our methodology.
paraphrase: Internal and external expert feedback on the report and the CEO/RSO conclusions will generally be solicited to inform future methodology refinements.

context_stem: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
excerpt: For high-stakes issues, however, the CEO and RSO will likely solicit internal and external feedback on the report prior to making any decisions.
paraphrase: For high-stakes issues, the CEO and RSO will likely seek internal and external feedback before making decisions.

context_stem: The process for making such a determination is as follows:
excerpt: If the CEO and RSO decide to proceed with deployment, they will share their decision–as well as the underlying Capability Report, internal feedback, and any external feedback–with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust before moving forward.
paraphrase: If deployment proceeds, the CEO and RSO will share the decision, Capability Report, and any feedback with the Board of Directors and Long-Term Benefit Trust before moving forward.

excerpt: In the case where the capability assessment shows a model is just barely below the threshold, the Responsible Scaling Officer may choose to limit further training to some amount less than the default 4x Effective Compute increase until ASL-3 measures are in place, in order to limit risk.
paraphrase: If a model is just barely below threshold, the RSO may limit further training below the default 4x Effective Compute increase until ASL-3 measures are ready, to limit risk.

excerpt: If, however, we determine we are unable to make the required showing, we will act as though the model has surpassed the Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: If the required showing cannot be made, the model will be treated as having surpassed the Capability Threshold.

excerpt: This means that we will (1) upgrade to the ASL-3 Required Safeguards (see Section 4) and (2) conduct follow-up a capability assessment to confirm that the ASL-4 Standard is not necessary (see Section 5).
paraphrase: This requires upgrading to ASL-3 Required Safeguards and conducting a follow-up capability assessment to confirm ASL-4 is unnecessary.

excerpt: To determine whether the measures we have adopted satisfy the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, we will conduct a safeguards assessment.
paraphrase: Anthropic will conduct a safeguards assessment to determine whether adopted measures satisfy ASL-3 Required Safeguards.

excerpt: As noted, the Required Safeguards for each Capability Threshold are specified in Section 2.
paraphrase: The Required Safeguards for each Capability Threshold are specified elsewhere in Section 2.

excerpt: We will document our implementation of the Required Safeguards in a Safeguards Report.
paraphrase: Anthropic will document its implementation of Required Safeguards in a Safeguards Report.

excerpt: When a model must meet the ASL-3 Deployment Standard, we will evaluate whether the measures we have implemented make us robust to persistent attempts to misuse the capability in question.
paraphrase: For models requiring the ASL-3 Deployment Standard, Anthropic will assess whether implemented measures provide robustness against sustained misuse attempts.

excerpt: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
paraphrase: Anthropic lists criteria that must be satisfied to demonstrate compliance with the ASL-3 Deployment Standard.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Threat modeling: Make a compelling case that the set of threats and the vectors through which an adversary could catastrophically misuse the deployed system have been sufficiently mapped out, and will commit to revising as necessary over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic must convincingly demonstrate that threats and misuse vectors have been mapped out and commit to revising this over time.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Defense in depth: Use a "defense in depth" approach by building a series of defensive layers, each designed to catch misuse attempts that might pass through previous barriers.
paraphrase: Anthropic will build multiple layers of defense to catch misuse attempts that evade earlier barriers.

context_stem: Defense in depth: Use a "defense in depth" approach by building a series of defensive layers...
excerpt: As an example, this might entail achieving a high overall recall rate using harm refusal techniques. This is an area of active research, and new technologies may be added when ready.
paraphrase: An example is achieving high recall via harm refusal techniques, and this is an evolving research area where new methods may be incorporated.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Red-teaming: Conduct red-teaming that demonstrates that threat actors with realistic access levels and resources are highly unlikely to be able to consistently elicit information from any generally accessible systems that greatly increases their ability to cause catastrophic harm relative to other available tools.
paraphrase: Anthropic must conduct red-teaming showing realistic threat actors are highly unlikely to gain catastrophic-harm-enabling information beyond what other tools provide.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Rapid remediation: Show that any compromises of the deployed system, such as jailbreaks or other attack pathways, will be identified and remediated promptly enough to prevent the overall system from meaningfully increasing an adversary's ability to cause catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: Anthropic must show that system compromises will be found and fixed quickly enough to prevent meaningful increases in catastrophic-harm capability.

context_stem: Rapid remediation: Show that any compromises of the deployed system...will be identified and remediated promptly enough...
excerpt: Example techniques could include rapid vulnerability patching, the ability to escalate to law enforcement when appropriate, and any necessary retention of logs for these activities.
paraphrase: Example remediation techniques include rapid patching, law enforcement escalation, and necessary log retention.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Monitoring: Prespecify empirical evidence that would show the system is operating within the accepted risk range and define a process for reviewing the system's performance on a reasonable cadence.
paraphrase: Anthropic must define in advance the evidence indicating the system is within acceptable risk and set a review process cadence.

excerpt: Process examples include monitoring responses to jailbreak bounties, doing historical analysis or background monitoring, and any necessary retention of logs for these activities.
paraphrase: Examples of monitoring processes include jailbreak bounty response monitoring, historical/background analysis, and log retention.

excerpt: There may be a substantial period during which models are not demonstrably close to the Capability Threshold, but we nevertheless are unable to rule out the risk to our satisfaction, and thus choose to implement the Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic may implement Required Safeguards even before a model is demonstrably close to the Capability Threshold, if risk cannot be ruled out confidently.

excerpt: This criterion does not attempt to specify the exact red-teaming protocol (e.g., number of hours, level of access, or pass-fail criteria).
paraphrase: The red-teaming criterion does not specify exact protocol details like hours, access level, or pass-fail thresholds.

excerpt: Setting a principled pass-fail threshold will depend on other factors, such as the quality of our monitoring and ability to respond to jailbreaks rapidly.
paraphrase: The pass-fail threshold for red-teaming depends on factors like monitoring quality and jailbreak response speed.

excerpt: Due to the likely ease of bypassing or removing safeguards via fine-tuning, it may be difficult or impossible for these red-teaming tests to pass if weights are released or if unmoderated fine-tuning access is provided to untrusted users.
paraphrase: Because fine-tuning can easily bypass safeguards, red-teaming tests may fail to pass if weights are released or unmoderated fine-tuning access is given to untrusted users.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Trusted users: Establish criteria for determining when it may be appropriate to share a version of the model with reduced safeguards with trusted users.
paraphrase: Anthropic must set criteria for when sharing a reduced-safeguard model version with trusted users is appropriate.

context_stem: Trusted users: Establish criteria for determining when it may be appropriate to share a version of the model with reduced safeguards...
excerpt: In addition, demonstrate that an alternative set of controls will provide equivalent levels of assurance. This could include a sufficient combination of user vetting, secure access controls, monitoring, log retention, and incident response protocols.
paraphrase: Anthropic must also demonstrate that alternative controls—such as vetting, access controls, monitoring, log retention, and incident response—provide equivalent assurance.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Third-party environments: Document how all relevant models will meet the criteria above, even if they are deployed in a third-party partner's environment that may have a different set of safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic must document how models meet the above criteria even when deployed in third-party partner environments with differing safeguards.

excerpt: When a model must meet the ASL-3 Security Standard, we will evaluate whether the measures we have implemented make us highly protected against most attackers' attempts at stealing model weights.
paraphrase: For models requiring the ASL-3 Security Standard, Anthropic will evaluate whether implemented measures provide strong protection against most weight-theft attempts.

excerpt: We consider the following groups in scope: hacktivists, criminal hacker groups, organized cybercrime groups, terrorist organizations, corporate espionage teams, internal employees, and state-sponsored programs that use broad-based and non-targeted techniques (i.e., not novel attack chains).
paraphrase: The in-scope threat actors for ASL-3 Security Standard include hacktivists, criminal groups, terrorists, corporate espionage teams, insiders, and state programs using non-novel techniques.

excerpt: The following groups are out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard because further testing (as discussed below) should confirm that the model would not meaningfully increase their ability to do harm: state-sponsored programs that specifically target us (e.g., through novel attack chains or insider compromise) and a small number (~10) of non-state actors with state-level resourcing or backing that are capable of developing novel attack chains that utilize 0-day attacks.
paraphrase: Out-of-scope threat actors include state programs specifically targeting Anthropic and roughly ten non-state actors with state-level capability for novel attack chains and zero-day exploits.

excerpt: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
paraphrase: Anthropic lists criteria needed to demonstrate compliance with the ASL-3 Security Standard.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Threat modeling: Follow risk governance best practices, such as use of the MITRE ATT&CK Framework to establish the relationship between the identified threats, sensitive assets, attack vectors and, in doing so, sufficiently capture the resulting risks that must be addressed to protect model weights from theft attempts.
paraphrase: Anthropic must follow risk governance practices like the MITRE ATT&CK Framework to map threats, assets, and vectors relevant to weight theft.

context_stem: Threat modeling: Follow risk governance best practices...
excerpt: As part of this requirement, we should specify our plans for revising the resulting threat model over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic should specify plans to revise the threat model over time.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Security frameworks: Align to and, as needed, extend industry-standard security frameworks for addressing identified risks, such as disclosure of sensitive information, tampering with accounts and assets, and unauthorized elevation of privileges with the appropriate controls. This includes:
paraphrase: Anthropic must align with and extend industry-standard security frameworks to address risks like data disclosure, tampering, and privilege escalation.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and, as needed, extend industry-standard security frameworks... This includes:
excerpt: Perimeters and access controls: Building strong perimeters and access controls around sensitive assets to ensure AI models and critical systems are protected from unauthorized access.
paraphrase: Sub-item on building strong perimeters and access controls to protect AI models and critical systems from unauthorized access.

context_stem: Perimeters and access controls: Building strong perimeters and access controls around sensitive assets...
excerpt: We expect this will include a combination of physical security, encryption, cloud security, infrastructure policy, access management, and weight access minimization and monitoring.
paraphrase: Expected components include physical security, encryption, cloud security, infrastructure policy, access management, and weight access minimization/monitoring.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and, as needed, extend industry-standard security frameworks... This includes:
excerpt: Lifecycle security: Securing links in the chain of systems and software used to develop models, to prevent compromised components from being introduced and to ensure only trusted code and hardware is used.
paraphrase: Sub-item on securing the development supply chain to prevent compromised components and ensure trusted code/hardware use.

context_stem: Lifecycle security: Securing links in the chain of systems and software used to develop models...
excerpt: We expect this will include a combination of software inventory, supply chain security, artifact integrity, binary authorization, hardware procurement, and secure research development lifecycle.
paraphrase: Expected components include software inventory, supply chain security, artifact integrity, binary authorization, hardware procurement, and secure R&D lifecycle.

excerpt: We will implement robust insider risk controls to mitigate most insider risk, but consider mitigating risks from highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders to be out of scope for ASL-3.
paraphrase: Robust insider risk controls will address most insider threats, but highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders are out of scope for ASL-3.

excerpt: We are committed to further enhancing these protections as a part of our ASL-4 preparations.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to enhancing insider protections further as part of ASL-4 preparations.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and, as needed, extend industry-standard security frameworks... This includes:
excerpt: Monitoring: Proactively identifying and mitigating threats through ongoing and effective monitoring, testing for vulnerabilities, and laying traps for potential attackers.
paraphrase: Sub-item on proactive threat identification via monitoring, vulnerability testing, and attacker traps.

context_stem: Monitoring: Proactively identifying and mitigating threats through ongoing and effective monitoring...
excerpt: We expect this will include a combination of endpoint patching, product security testing, log management, asset monitoring, and intruder deception techniques.
paraphrase: Expected components include endpoint patching, product security testing, log management, asset monitoring, and deception techniques.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and, as needed, extend industry-standard security frameworks... This includes:
excerpt: Resourcing: Investing sufficient resources in security.
paraphrase: Sub-item requiring sufficient investment of resources in security.

context_stem: Resourcing: Investing sufficient resources in security.
excerpt: We expect meeting this standard of security to require roughly 5-10% of employees being dedicated to security and security-adjacent work.
paraphrase: Meeting the security standard is expected to require about 5-10% of employees dedicated to security-related work.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and, as needed, extend industry-standard security frameworks... This includes:
excerpt: Existing guidance: Aligning where appropriate with existing guidance on securing model weights, including Securing AI Model Weights, Preventing Theft and Misuse of Frontier Models (2024); security recommendations like Deploying AI Systems Securely (CISA/NSA/FBI/ASD/CCCS/GCSB /GCHQ), ISO 42001, CSA's AI Safety Initiative, and CoSAI; and standards frameworks like SSDF, SOC 2, NIST 800-53.
paraphrase: Anthropic will align with existing external guidance and standards on securing model weights, including named frameworks and agency recommendations.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Audits: Develop plans to (1) audit and assess the design and implementation of the security program and (2) share these findings (and updates on any remediation efforts) with management on an appropriate cadence.
paraphrase: Anthropic must develop plans to audit the security program and share findings with management regularly.

context_stem: Audits: Develop plans to (1) audit and assess the design and implementation of the security program...
excerpt: We expect this to include independent validation of threat modeling and risk assessment results; a sampling-based audit of the operating effectiveness of the defined controls; periodic, broadly scoped, and independent testing with expert red-teamers who are industry-renowned and have been recognized in competitive challenges.
paraphrase: The audit is expected to include independent validation of threat models, sampling-based control audits, and periodic independent testing by renowned expert red-teamers.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Third-party environments: Document how all relevant models will meet the criteria above, even if they are deployed in a third-party partner's environment that may have a different set of safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic must document how models meet the above security criteria even when deployed in third-party partner environments with different safeguards.

excerpt: If, after the evaluations above, we determine that we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, then we may proceed with deploying and training models above the Capability Threshold, provided we have also conducted a follow-up capability assessment.
paraphrase: If ASL-3 Required Safeguards are confirmed met, Anthropic may proceed with training/deploying models above the Capability Threshold, contingent on a follow-up capability assessment.

excerpt: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
paraphrase: Anthropic outlines the process for determining ASL-3 Required Safeguards compliance below.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: First, we will compile a Safeguards Report for each Required Safeguard that documents our implementation of the measures above, makes an affirmative case for why we have satisfied them, and advances recommendations on deployment decisions.
paraphrase: Anthropic will first compile a Safeguards Report per Required Safeguard documenting implementation, justifying compliance, and recommending deployment decisions.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: The Safeguards Report(s) will be escalated to the CEO and the Responsible Scaling Officer, who will (1) make the ultimate determination as to whether we have satisfied the Required Safeguards and (2) decide any deployment-related issues.
paraphrase: Safeguards Reports go to the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer, who determine compliance and decide deployment issues.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: In general, as noted in Sections 7.1.4 and 7.2.2, we will solicit both internal and external expert feedback on the report as well as the CEO and RSO's conclusions to inform future refinements to our methodology.
paraphrase: Anthropic will generally seek internal and external expert feedback on the report and leadership conclusions to refine methodology.

context_stem: In general...we will solicit both internal and external expert feedback...
excerpt: For high-stakes issues, however, the CEO and RSO will likely solicit internal and external feedback on the report prior to making any decisions.
paraphrase: For high-stakes issues, the CEO and RSO will likely gather feedback before deciding.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: If the CEO and RSO decide to proceed with deployment and training, they will share their decision–as well as the underlying Capability Report, internal feedback, and any external feedback–with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust before moving forward.
paraphrase: If deployment/training is approved, the CEO and RSO will share the decision and supporting materials with the Board and the Long-Term Benefit Trust beforehand.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: After the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are approved, they will be revisited and re-approved at least annually to re-affirm their suitability and sound implementation.
paraphrase: Approved ASL-3 Required Safeguards will be reviewed and re-approved at least once a year.

excerpt: If, however, we are unable to make the showing required above, we will restrict model deployment and further scaling.
paraphrase: If Anthropic cannot demonstrate compliance, it will restrict model deployment and further scaling.

excerpt: In parallel with upgrading a model to the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, we will conduct a follow-up capability assessment to determine that the model's capability falls sufficiently far away from the Capability Thresholds that would trigger ASL-4 Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Alongside upgrading to ASL-3 Required Safeguards, Anthropic will assess whether model capability is sufficiently distant from ASL-4-triggering thresholds.

excerpt: We will update this policy with the Capability Thresholds for the ASL-4 Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic will update the policy to include Capability Thresholds for ASL-4 Required Safeguards.

excerpt: We are currently working on defining any further Capability Thresholds that would mandate ASL-4 Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Anthropic is currently working to define additional Capability Thresholds that would require ASL-4 Required Safeguards.

excerpt: Our update may not include all possible risks; we will prioritize capabilities that are likely to emerge earlier in frontier models.
paraphrase: The future update may not cover every risk, and Anthropic will prioritize capabilities expected to emerge earlier in frontier models.

excerpt: As noted, before deploying any model that passes the Capability Thresholds for the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, we will conduct a capability assessment against the forthcoming Capability Thresholds for the ASL-4 Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Before deploying any model exceeding ASL-3 Capability Thresholds, Anthropic will assess it against upcoming ASL-4 Capability Thresholds.

excerpt: We will follow the procedures outlined in Section 3.
paraphrase: Anthropic will follow the procedures described in Section 3.

excerpt: To summarize the commitments and procedures outlined above, we may deploy or store a model if either of the following criteria are met: (1) the model's capabilities are sufficiently far away from the existing Capability Thresholds, making the current ASL-2 Standard appropriate; or (2) the model's capabilities have surpassed the existing Capabilities Threshold, but we have implemented the ASL-3 Required Safeguards and confirmed that the model is sufficiently far away from the next set of Capability Thresholds as to make the model ASL-3 Standard appropriate.
paraphrase: Anthropic may deploy or store a model if it remains sufficiently below current Capability Thresholds (ASL-2 appropriate), or if it exceeds thresholds but ASL-3 Required Safeguards are implemented and it's sufficiently below the next thresholds (ASL-3 appropriate).

excerpt: We may also continue to train more capable models, conducting preliminary and comprehensive assessments as before.
paraphrase: Anthropic may continue training more capable models while conducting the same preliminary and comprehensive assessments as before.

excerpt: In any scenario where we determine that a model requires ASL-3 Required Safeguards but we are unable to implement them immediately, we will act promptly to reduce interim risk to acceptable levels until the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are in place:
paraphrase: If a model requires ASL-3 Required Safeguards that cannot be implemented immediately, Anthropic will act promptly to reduce interim risk until the safeguards are ready.

context_stem: In any scenario where we determine that a model requires ASL-3 Required Safeguards but we are unable to implement them immediately...
excerpt: Interim measures: The CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer may approve the use of interim measures that provide the same level of assurance as the relevant ASL-3 Standard but are faster or simpler to implement.
paraphrase: The CEO and RSO may approve interim measures offering equivalent assurance to the ASL-3 Standard but that are quicker or easier to implement.

context_stem: Interim measures: The CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer may approve the use of interim measures...
excerpt: In the deployment context, such measures might include blocking model responses, downgrading to a less-capable model in a particular domain, or increasing the sensitivity of automated monitoring.
paraphrase: In deployment, interim measures might include blocking responses, downgrading to a less capable model in a domain, or increasing monitoring sensitivity.

context_stem: Interim measures: The CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer may approve the use of interim measures...
excerpt: In the security context, an example of such a measure would be storing the model weights in a single-purpose, isolated network that meets the ASL-3 Standard.
paraphrase: In the security context, an example interim measure is storing model weights in an isolated, single-purpose network meeting the ASL-3 Standard.

context_stem: Interim measures: The CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer may approve the use of interim measures...
excerpt: In either case, the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer will share their plan with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust.
paraphrase: In either deployment or security context, the CEO and RSO will share their interim plan with the Board and the Long-Term Benefit Trust.

excerpt: Less prescriptive evaluation methodology: We have replaced some specifics in our previous testing methodology (e.g., using 1% of compute for elicitation or creating a 6x buffer), with more general requirements to (a) match expected efforts of potential adversaries and (b) provide informal estimates of how further scaling and research developments will impact model capabilities and performance on the same tasks.
paraphrase: Specific prior methodology elements like 1% compute for elicitation or a 6x buffer were replaced with general requirements to match adversary effort and estimate future scaling impacts.

excerpt: We have found that specific methodologies may become outdated when new research developments are introduced.
paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.

excerpt: Although still an aspirational goal, the science of evaluations is not currently mature enough to make confident predictions about the precise buffer we should require between current models and a Capability Threshold.
paraphrase: Precise buffer requirements remain an aspirational goal since evaluation science is not yet mature enough for confident predictions.

excerpt: More outcome-focused safeguard requirements: We have updated our ASL-3 safeguards requirements to be less prescriptive and more outcome-focused.
paraphrase: ASL-3 safeguard requirements were updated to be less prescriptive and more focused on outcomes.

excerpt: Rather than detailing specific operational and technical safeguards, we now specify the overall security or deployment standards and requirements for meeting them. This is to allow us to adapt our safeguards more flexibly as our understanding of risks and possible safeguards improves.
paraphrase: Instead of specifying detailed safeguards, the policy now sets overall standards and requirements, allowing flexible adaptation as understanding improves.

locator: Changelog / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models: We have clarified which actors are in and out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard.
paraphrase: The update clarifies which actors are in or out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard.

locator: Changelog / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: We also removed the commitment to protect against scaled attacks and distillation attacks from the ASL-2 Security standard.
paraphrase: The commitment to protect against scaled and distillation attacks was removed from the ASL-2 Security standard.

locator: Changelog / Clarified ASL-3 and ASL-2 security threat models
excerpt: While distillation remains a concern for more capable models, models stored under ASL-2 safeguards have not yet reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.
paraphrase: Distillation still concerns more capable models, but ASL-2-stored models have not reached potentially harmful Capability Thresholds.

locator: Changelog / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users: We have updated the ASL-3 Deployment Standard to allow for different levels of safeguards based on deployment context.
paraphrase: The ASL-3 Deployment Standard now allows differing safeguard levels depending on deployment context.

locator: Changelog / Clarified requirements for deployments with trusted users
excerpt: For any general access systems, we still require passing intensive red-teaming. For internal use, safety testing and deployments to sufficiently trusted users, we will instead require a combination of access controls and monitoring.
paraphrase: General access systems still require intensive red-teaming, while internal use and trusted-user deployments require access controls and monitoring instead.

locator: Changelog / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
excerpt: New Capability and Safeguards Reports: We have introduced Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports.
paraphrase: Capability Reports and Safeguard Reports were introduced as new instruments.

locator: Changelog / New Capability and Safeguards Reports
excerpt: We expect that aggregating all the available evidence about model capabilities will provide decision makers with a more complete picture of the overall level of risk and improve our ability to solicit feedback on our work.
paraphrase: Aggregating evidence via these reports is expected to give decision-makers a fuller risk picture and improve feedback solicitation.

excerpt: Internal and external accountability: We have made a number of changes to our previous "procedural commitments."
paraphrase: Several changes were made to the previous procedural commitments.

excerpt: These include expanding the duties of the Responsible Scaling Officer; adding internal critique and external expert input on capability and safeguard assessments; new procedures related to internal governance; and maintaining a public page for overviews of past Capability and Safeguard Reports, RSP-related updates, and future plans.
paraphrase: Changes include expanded RSO duties, added internal critique and external input on assessments, new internal governance procedures, and a public page for report overviews, updates, and plans.
